subject: Emotions
title: Inflammation and Sadness
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Inflammation and Sadness.

hook.text: When you have the flu, you feel sad and withdrawn. That's not coincidence—it's inflammation hitting the brain.

buildup.text: Cytokines—immune signaling molecules—cross into the brain and alter mood, energy, and motivation.

discovery.text: About 30% of depressed patients show elevated inflammation markers. Their sadness may be immune-driven.

twist.text: Anti-inflammatory drugs reduced depression symptoms in clinical trials. Treating the body treated the mind.

climax.text: This means some sadness isn't psychological at all. It's your immune system changing your mood.

punchline.text: Sometimes the cure for sadness is in the body, not the mind.

quiz.question: What percentage of depressed patients show elevated inflammation?
